2. Perused the record.
3. sentences.text: Learned counsel for applicants submits that applicant 1 is the husband of first informant-opposite party 2.
Marriage of applicant 1 was solemnized with first informant-opposite party 2.

However,
relationship in between applicant 1 and opposite party 2 became strained on account of marital discord.
Consequently criminal proceedings came to be initiated by opposite party 2 against applicant 1 and his family members.

During the pendency of aforementioned criminal proceedings,
applicant 1 and opposite party 2 themselves aggrieved to terminate their marital relationship.

Resultantly, H.M.A. No. 1440 of 2021 (Kamlesh Vs. Suman Vishwakarma) under Section 13B(1) of Hindu Marriage Act came to be instituted in the court of Principal Judge, Family Court-I,
Gorakhpur.

5. He has then invited the attention of the Court to the paragraph 3 of plaint of above-mentioned divorce petition and on basis thereof, he submits that proceedings of above-mentioned criminal case are liable to be quashed by this Court.

6. He has then referred to the judgement of Supreme Court in Shlok Bhardwaj V. Runika Bhardwaj (2015) 2 SCC 721 wherein it has been held that compromise entered into by the parties in a matrimonial dispute, must be construed as an effective compromise so as to bring to an end all dispute between the parties.

entities.text: Shlok Bhardwaj V. Runika Bhardwaj (2015) 2 SCC 721
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: On the above premise, it is urged that the entire proceedings of aforementioned criminal case are liable to be quashed by this Court.
According to the learned counsel for applicants, the dispute between the parties is basically a matrimonial dispute and not a crime against society.

In view of the settlement arrived at between applicant 1 and opposite party 2,
which is manifest from the proceedings under Section 13B(1) of the Hindu Marriage Act, no useful purpose shall be served in prolonging the proceedings of aforementioned criminal case.
In fact, the continuation of the proceedings of above-mentioned criminal case will itself cause injustice to the parties.
On the above premise, it is urged that the entire proceedings of above-mentioned criminal case are liable to be quashed by this Court.
7. Per contra, the learned A.G.A. has opposed the present application.
However, he could not dislodge the factual/legal submissions urged by the learned counsel for applicants.

He, however,
submits that once the marital relationship in between applicant 1 and first informant-opposite party 2 has itself being agreed to be terminated, no useful purpose shall be served in prolonging the proceedings of above-mentioned criminal case.
8. Mr. Chandraveer Singh, Advocate, holding brief of Mr. Hemant Kumar Dubey, the learned counsel representing first informant-opposite party 2 also does not oppose the present application.
He submits that since compromise has been entered into by the parties, therefore, he has no objection, in case, the proceedings of aforementioned criminal case are quashed by this Court.

9. Having heard, the learned counsel for applicants, the learned A.G.A. for State, Mr. Hemant Kumar Dubey, the learned counsel representing first informant-opposite party 2 and upon perusal Kamlesh Vishwakarma And 10 Others vs State Of U.P. And Another on 15 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/56054904/

entities.text: Kamlesh Vishwakarma And 10 Others vs State Of U.P. And Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: of record, this Court finds that considering the facts and circumstances of case, submissions made by counsel for parties and the material on record, this court is of considered opinion that dispute between parties is a purely private dispute and not a crime against society.
Moreover, during pendency of present application, parties have already compromised their dispute.
Compromise so entered into by parties has been acted upon .
As such, on date no difference exists between parties.
Consequently, no useful purpose shall be served in prolonging the proceedings of above mentioned case.
In view of compromise entered into by the parties, chances of conviction of accused applicants is remote and bleak.
As such continuation of proceedings would itself cause injustice to parties.
The trial would only entail loss of judicial time in a futile pursuit particularly when torrents of litigation drown the courts with an unimaginable flood of dockets.
10. In view of above, present application succeeds and is liable to be allowed.
11. It is accordingly allowed.

12. Entire proceedings of theCase No. 24829 of 2022 (State Vs. Kamlesh and Others), under Sections 498A, 323, 504, 506 IPC and 3/4 Dowry Prohibition Act, Police Station-Gulriha,
District-Gorakhpur now pending in court of Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate-II, Gorakhpur are hereby quashed.
13. Cost made easy.
